accepted_facts: On a synthetic operator with the eigenvalue spectrum pinned EXACTLY (spectral radius 0.8500 at every step; max absolute deviation 0.0), the worst-case transient amplification sup_t||A^t|| grows from 0.850 to 994964.141 as the Henrici departure rises from 0 to 27.04 — the eigenvalues never move while the transient explodes.

Over a pool of 16 operators varying BOTH spectrum and non-normality, the Kreiss constant is a near-sufficient statistic for the (log) transient: R^2 0.991 on log Kreiss versus only 0.091 on the eigenvalue spectral radius (numerical radius 0.825, raw departure 0.727).

The raw non-normality scalar (Henrici departure) is NOT the right yardstick; PRO conceded this and named the pseudospectral object (Kreiss constant), which the Kreiss matrix theorem binds two-sidedly to transient growth.

At an IDENTICAL spectrum (radius 0.9) the non-normal delay-line chain (departure 5.94) had memory capacity 26.27 versus the normal operator's 33.82 — it remembered LESS, not more, so the memory half of the thesis is not supported.
rejected_or_quarantined_evidence: Both sides' first construction (a strictly-upper Schur perturbation) moved the spectrum it was meant to fix (spectral radius drifted from 0.85 to ~1.21); rejected in favour of a strictly BLOCK-upper perturbation that holds every eigenvalue fixed.
Several CON counter-examples were invalid: a 'shuffle' that fed back the same matrix, and a dense construction that overflowed in float64 and changed the spectrum.
The claim that this transfers to real biological sparse synaptic matrices: untested (synthetic operators only); quarantined as out of scope rather than treated as evidence either way.
argument_quality: PRO held the fixed-spectrum falsifier frame, repaired its own broken constructions (the spectrum-moving perturbation), and shifted the contest from a crude non-normality scalar to the pseudospectrum and Kreiss constant — the mathematically correct object. CON landed real hits (correctly flagging unpinned spectra and the crudeness of the departure scalar, and rightly insisting memory depends on structure, noise and readout), but several of its decisive counter-examples were invalid, so within the transcript it refined the remaining uncertainty rather than overturning PRO.
protocol_conduct: Decisive test pre-registered before compute and schema-valid; real, deterministic compute (numpy, seed 17) with exact float64 spectral-radius invariance (deviation 0.0); order-swap audit PASS (substantive call 'pro' on the natural run, 'unclear' when the side order was swapped); a verbosity-confound warning is flagged because CON wrote substantially more than PRO and length was not credited as merit.
evidence_quality: Real, deterministic, rerunnable compute, but on SYNTHETIC controlled-spectrum operators rather than biologically sampled connectomes. The decisive observable is a proxy (not paper-faithful) and establishes that non-normality is SUFFICIENT to govern transients at a fixed spectrum, not that real sparse synaptic matrices do so. The Kreiss constant is a finite-grid lower bound; memory capacity is measured in a simplified noisy linear reservoir whose readout and noise direction can change the result.

what_it_supports.statement: That at an identical eigenvalue spectrum, transient amplification is governed by non-normality — pinning the spectral radius at 0.85, the worst-case transient grows from 0.85 to ~10^6 as departure rises.
That the right yardstick is pseudospectral: the Kreiss constant explains 99% of the log transient variance while the eigenvalue spectral radius explains 9%.
That the eigenvalue spectrum is not a sufficient statistic for transients, and becomes numerically unreliable precisely when non-normality is high.

what_it_does_not_support.statement: That non-normality alone governs memory: at an identical spectrum the non-normal chain remembered less (26.27 vs 33.82), so the memory half overreaches.
That real biological sparse synaptic matrices live in this regime: synthetic sufficiency does not establish external validity.
Any discovery-level or data-level claim about the seed paper's empirics; the spectrum still sets the asymptotic fate (t->inf).

what_remains_open: Whether pseudospectral measures still dominate transient amplification and memory on biologically sampled sparse synaptic ensembles with the spectrum strictly controlled.
Whether a richer non-normality descriptor (beyond a single scalar) governs memory once structure, noise direction and readout are accounted for.
Whether the small finite-horizon and finite-grid approximations (sup over t=1..400; Kreiss on a 24x72 grid) materially affect the rank-ordering at higher non-normality.
permitted_wording: On synthetic operators with the spectrum held exactly fixed, non-normality was sufficient to drive transient amplification up by orders of magnitude while the eigenvalues did not move.
The Kreiss constant predicted the log transient far better than the spectral radius (R^2 0.991 vs 0.091) across operators varying both spectrum and non-normality.
PRO prevailed on argumentation; the substantive merits-call is split — well supported for transients, overreaching for memory — and the real-data version remains unclear pending a biological test.
forbidden_wording: Do not say this proves the claim that non-normality governs transients and memory in real synaptic matrices: the test is synthetic controlled-spectrum operators, not biological connectomes (доказывает тезис).
Do not say this establishes the claim on real data; it establishes only synthetic sufficiency for the transient half (устанавливает истинность тезиса).
Do not say this confirms the claim that non-normality governs memory — the memory test contradicts it (the chain remembered less at an identical spectrum) (подтверждает истинность тезиса).
Do not say this settles the question of whether the spectrum or the pseudospectrum governs real neural dynamics (окончательно решает вопрос).

Do not say this definitively shows or is a definitive result: the Kreiss dominance is a synthetic sufficiency probe, the memory half is unsupported, and external validity is untested (неопровержимо показывает / definitive).
Do not say the eigenvalue spectrum is useless: it still sets the asymptotic fate (t->inf); it is only an insufficient statistic for transients.
Do not write 'an AI proved' or 'model X beat model Y'; the sides are public roles and engine identities are withheld.
confidence_and_limitations: High confidence within a narrow scope on the transient half: at a spectrum pinned exactly at radius 0.85 the worst-case transient amplification rises by six orders of magnitude with non-normality (spectral-radius deviation 0.0), and the Kreiss constant is a near-sufficient statistic (R^2 0.991) while the spectral radius is nearly useless (0.091); the order-swap audit is stable with a substantive call of 'pro' naturally and 'unclear' swapped. Low confidence / not supported on the memory half: the non-normal chain stored less than the normal operator at the identical spectrum. Out of scope: no biologically sampled synaptic matrices, a finite-grid Kreiss lower bound, and a simplified noisy linear reservoir for memory. Genre: scout — a synthetic sufficiency probe, not a scientific_result.
